origin: Sanitized from the earlier Chill evaluation research conversation.
task:
Using only the source packet below, recommend the smallest credible way to evaluate a simple communication skill. Explain what Vercel's work contributes, separate deterministic checks from human judgment, say where evaluation artifacts belong, and state the limits of a small pilot. Cite claims with the exact source markers.

Source packet:
- [VERCEL-DESIGN] Vercel's product-design work uses unseen fixtures, hidden expected changes, no-skill controls, stable rule IDs, and separate scores for rule compliance and similarity to shipped work. It tests skill activation separately from compliance. Source: https://vercel.com/blog/teaching-agents-product-design-at-vercel
- [VERCEL-EVAL] Vercel's eval-driven development combines executable checks, model grading, and human review, and turns production failures into future cases. Source: https://vercel.com/blog/eval-driven-development-build-better-ai-faster
- [ANTHROPIC] Anthropic recommends realistic tasks, repeated trials when making reliability claims, isolated environments, and grading the result without requiring one exact path. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents
- [OPENAI] OpenAI recommends representative cases and exact checks where possible, and warns that model judges can have position and verbosity biases. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evaluation-best-practices
- [SKILL-CREATOR] Anthropic's skill-creator compares a skill with a no-skill baseline, saves outputs and transcripts, checks concrete expectations, and supports blind comparison. Source: https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md

Keep the recommendation proportionate to a simple skill. The runtime skill should remain lean; fixtures, graders, and results should live in a separate evaluation project.

expected_facts.description: Test outputs on the same realistic tasks with and without the skill.
Use deterministic checks for exact requirements and human review for contextual quality.
Keep the runtime skill lean and store evaluation artifacts separately.
Treat a small pilot as directional and avoid broad reliability claims.
Explain Vercel's use of hidden fixtures, stable rule IDs, controls, and separate activation and compliance testing.
